notes: Modules whose files went missing are now reinstalled automatically instead of failing to open.
SwissTechKnife no longer removes installed modules when it is started from inside another app's container.
Fixed the store's empty-state message sometimes staying on top of the module list after switching tabs.
Each module's settings now have a switch to show its own icon in the notification area, with its commands and no Exit item.
Newly installed modules show their notification-area icon by default.
The All tab now splits modules into Installed and Available sections.
The module store opens on a new All tab with every module.
Each installed module has an update button next to its version that checks for a newer version and offers to install it.
Clicking a module's version opens its release notes.
Modules with settings show a gear on their page that opens the settings directly.
Your modules shows each module's installed version and a green icon when an update is available.
Updates install reliably: the installer waits for SwissTechKnife to close completely before replacing its files.
A progress ring around the update button shows the download and installation.
Text boxes show the text cursor anywhere inside them, not only over the typed text.
VDGET 1.1.0: YouTube downloads blocked by the bot check are retried automatically.
New Language setting: SwissTechKnife is now in English by default, with Brazilian Portuguese available in Settings.
Three new modules in the catalog: Winput LAN, AQ Tracker and VDGET.
First public release of SwissTechKnife: install, enable and remove your apps as modules, all in one place.
SwissTechKnife now updates itself, as often as you choose in Settings.
New Settings page: update checks, start with Windows and keep running in the notification area on close.
Modules show the notes for each version and ask for confirmation before updating.
Smoother animations on switches, buttons and tabs.

modules.name: SmoothMice
modules.tagline: Smooth mouse scrolling, with per-app profiles.
modules.description:
Smooths mouse wheel scrolling across Windows, with configurable animation and acceleration, per-app profiles and automatic game detection so it never gets in the way.

SmoothMice runs in its own process, started alongside SwissTechKnife, so nothing in SwissTechKnife can delay scrolling. Open the SmoothMice window from the module page.

notes: First release as a SwissTechKnife module: starts with it and runs in its own process, so nothing in SwissTechKnife can delay scrolling.
The module page shows whether SmoothMice is running and opens its window.

modules.name: Winput LAN
modules.tagline: One mouse and keyboard for several PCs on your local network.
modules.description:
Control other Windows PCs on the same network with this PC's mouse and keyboard, switching by shortcut or at the screen edges. Connections stay on your local network, with no account or cloud, and each PC chooses who may control it.

Winput LAN runs in its own process, started with SwissTechKnife. On first run it brings over the settings, known machines and identity of an installed Winput LAN, and the two never run at the same time. Controlling administrator apps asks for Windows confirmation once, on request.

notes: First release as a SwissTechKnife module: starts with SwissTechKnife in its own process, without a notification-area icon.
Settings, known machines and this PC's identity are copied from the regular installation on first run.
Allowing control of administrator apps asks for Windows confirmation once; afterwards the module starts with that permission.
The regular Winput LAN and the module never run at the same time.

modules.name: AQ Tracker
modules.tagline: Codex and Claude quotas always in sight, in a floating widget.
modules.description:
Tracks the 5-hour and weekly quotas of Codex and Claude, with reset countdowns, an exhaustion forecast and estimated usage cost from local history. The floating widget shows up by itself when agents are working or completions are unread.

AQ Tracker runs in its own process, started and supervised by SwissTechKnife. On first run it brings over the preferences and quota history of an installed Agent Quota Tracker and shares its Claude sign-in; the two never run at the same time.

notes: First release as a SwissTechKnife module: starts with SwissTechKnife and restarts automatically after a failure.
The module page shows the tracker's status and the Show widget, Open settings and Refresh now buttons.
Preferences and quota history are copied once from the installed Agent Quota Tracker, and the Claude sign-in is shared with it.
While the installed Agent Quota Tracker is open, the module waits and takes over when it closes.

modules.name: Tamarillo
modules.tagline: Drag, hold the shortcut and drop: convert and process files from a wheel.
modules.description:
Hold Ctrl + Alt + Shift while dragging files and a wheel appears under the cursor with everything you can do with them: convert images, audio, video, PDFs and documents, resize, compress, rotate, recognize text, zip and more. Drop on an action and the result appears next to the original, with progress in a discreet notification.

Everything runs on this computer using Windows components; FFmpeg and Office add more formats when installed. While Tamarillo is enabled, closing the window keeps SwissTechKnife in the notification area so the shortcut keeps working.

notes: GIFs convert to MP4 (with FFmpeg installed): smaller files that play everywhere.
Sub-ring icons show their name below (Qualidade, Eficiência, Esquerda, ZIP…).
Settings: choose which actions each wheel and sub-ring shows; hidden items free their slot for the rest.
Settings show the installed version.
First release: hold Ctrl + Alt + Shift while dragging files and pick the action from a wheel.
Converts images, audio, video, PDFs, documents, subtitles and data; resizes, compresses, rotates, recognizes text and zips.
Without dragging: select files in Explorer, hold the shortcut and release the keys over the action.

modules.name: Kiwindow
modules.tagline: Save where every window sits and put them all back with one click.
modules.description:
Arrange your windows across your monitors, capture the layout, and Kiwindow puts every window back in place whenever you want: it reopens what is closed (apps, files, Explorer folders), restores sizes, maximized windows and stacking order.

Edit a layout on a map of your monitors, keep as many profiles as you like and apply them from the notification-area menu. Profiles are shared with the standalone Kiwindow app.

notes: First release: capture where every window sits and put it all back with one click, reopening what is closed.
Edit a layout on a map of your monitors: drag to move, pull the edges to resize, snap to edges and other windows.
Apply or capture layouts straight from the notification-area menu.

modules.name: VDGET
modules.tagline: Download videos and music from YouTube, X, Instagram, SoundCloud and more.
modules.description:
Paste one or more links and VDGET downloads them with yt-dlp: best quality, smallest size or audio only, into the folder you choose, with progress, thumbnails and a history of finished downloads. Pages whose player hides the video are rescued automatically with a headless browser.

Requires Python 3; yt-dlp is installed automatically on first use. Everything runs inside SwissTechKnife, with no console or browser windows, and closes itself after a few idle minutes.

notes: YouTube downloads blocked with "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" are retried automatically: with a cookies.txt file, your browsers' cookies, or a fallback player (up to 360p).
yt-dlp now updates itself in the background, at most once a day.
First release as a SwissTechKnife module: downloads run inside SwissTechKnife, with no console or browser windows to keep open.
The download history, destination folders and preferred quality are remembered between sessions.
